nodes.text: My head hurts.
Where... am I?
I remember logging in.
A message. A warning.
Then-
Everything went dark.
This place... it does not feel real.
Or maybe... it feels too real.
Someone brought me here.
And I need to figure out why.
Before it is too late.
The room shifts again.
Same stone. Same silence.
Those markers are waiting for answers.
This place checks what I know before it opens the next path.
I need to read carefully.
Guessing will only make this harder.
So this is how it works.
Those markers were not random.
Each one tested what I would trust.
What I would ignore.
And what I would check first.
More paths. More traps.
Nothing here is placed by accident.
If something looks harmless...
I still need to inspect it.
The air feels heavier here.
These guardians are not guarding doors.
They are guarding habits.
Weak passwords. Reused passwords. Missing second factors.
If I need to type a password here, it must be fictional.
No real secrets. Not in a place built to test me.
I need to remember the first fictional password exactly.
The final guardian may ask for proof that I remember it.
This chamber is infected.
Those things are not just wandering.
I cannot fight malware head-on.
I can block when it strikes, then reach the scanner angel.
Wrong answers still hurt too.
Reach each angel. Quarantine the malware zone by zone.
This place is quieter than the others.
That makes it worse.
The danger here will not always look like a trap.
It may sound urgent. Helpful. Familiar. Official.
The people walking these halls may approach me before I am ready.
Every answer I give can change how much this place trusts my judgment.
Slow down. Verify the request. Never hand over secrets just because someone pressures me.
This room feels different.
The fragments are not just memories. They are evidence.
Four responders are trapped behind the seals.
Identify. Contain. Eradicate. Recover.
If malware closes in, I block and keep moving toward the scanner.
If I free the responders, they can break the core's guards.
Then the last question is whether I can write the report that gets me out.
The core stops fighting.
It was never a monster. It was the unfinished incident report.
Every room was a damaged record of the same attack.
Unsafe trust opened the path. Weak credentials widened it. Malware spread through it. Social pressure hid it.
The only way out is to finish the response.
Write the report. Close the incident.
The lever locks into place.
The sparks fade. The core is quiet.
Now I understand where I was.
Inside a reconstruction. A training system built from the incident itself.
It did not need me to defeat the attack.
It needed me to respond correctly.
Incident closed.
The report is complete.
The source was identified.
The damage was contained.
The threat was removed.
The system was recovered.
And the lesson was written down.
Incident closed.
Awareness begins before the next click.
